skill.name: forensics-osquery
skill.description: Use osquery to investigate endpoint activity, collect forensic evidence, and build detection queries across Linux, macOS, and Windows systems.
skill.summary: Investigate endpoints with osquery SQL queries for incident response and threat hunting.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: AI review adjudicated all 286 static alerts as false positives caused by osquery detection strings, query filters, and Markdown examples. No evidence found of prompt injection, automatic malware execution, or data exfiltration intent. The skill remains sensitive because authorized osquery workflows can collect privileged endpoint evidence.

remediation.issue: Sensitive endpoint evidence can be exposed in query results.
remediation.suggestion: Keep authorization, encryption, sanitization, and access logging guidance near every pack usage workflow.

remediation.issue: Credential-access queries can produce sensitive metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Document expected outputs and require review before sharing raw exports outside the response team.

remediation.issue: Broad scheduled queries can create operational noise.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend lab testing, result limits, and environment-specific allowlists before fleet deployment.

content.value_statement: Incident responders need fast endpoint evidence without switching tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through osquery triage, hunting, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Provides osquery workflows for process, network, file, user, and persistence analysis.
Maps common investigations to MITRE ATT&CK-oriented osquery queries.
Includes query packs for triage, persistence, lateral movement, and credential access detection.
Explains osqueryd deployment, scheduling, logging, and service management basics.
Highlights platform differences across Linux, macOS, and Windows osquery tables.
Offers guidance for evidence handling, query tuning, and SIEM integration.
limitations: Requires osquery or osqueryd to be installed on the target endpoint.
Some tables and results require root or administrator privileges.
Coverage depends on operating system support and enabled event collection.
The skill does not validate findings against live threat intelligence by itself.

use_cases.title: Rapid Endpoint Triage
use_cases.description: Collect process, login, network, and file metadata after an alert.

use_cases.title: MITRE-Based Threat Hunting
use_cases.description: Translate a suspected ATT&CK technique into osquery checks for endpoint artifacts.

use_cases.title: Fleet Monitoring Design
use_cases.description: Build scheduled osqueryd packs for persistence, credential access, and lateral movement indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Start Endpoint Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage on one suspected host.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the forensics-osquery skill to plan initial endpoint triage. Focus on processes, users, network connections, and recent files.

prompt_templates.title: Hunt Persistence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the forensics-osquery skill to create a persistence hunting workflow for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Explain each result.

prompt_templates.title: Map One Technique
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the forensics-osquery skill to map MITRE ATT&CK T1003 to artifacts, osquery checks, and evidence handling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Monitoring Pack
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the forensics-osquery skill to design an osqueryd pack for lateral movement and credential access. Include tuning and review steps.

output: A triage checklist for processes, users, network connections, persistence, and recent file activity.
Suggested osquery areas to inspect and ways to interpret abnormal results.
Evidence handling notes for timestamps, exports, and analyst actions.

output_examples.input: Create a hunt for suspicious PowerShell activity.
output: A hunt plan tied to Windows process telemetry and suspicious command-line indicators.
Expected benign sources to exclude during review.
Follow-up pivots for parent processes, network connections, and persistence artifacts.

output_examples.input: Prepare osqueryd monitoring for endpoint fleet coverage.
output: A deployment checklist for configuration, packs, logging, and service management.
Review points for query cost, data sensitivity, and role-based access.
A rollout sequence from lab testing to limited production deployment.

best_practices: Run privileged queries only on systems where you have explicit authorization.
Store exported results in encrypted locations with access logging and retention limits.
Test scheduled queries in a lab before enabling them on production endpoints.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad file or process queries without scope limits on production fleets.
Do not share raw osquery results before removing secrets and personal data.
Do not treat query matches as confirmed compromise without analyst validation.

faq.question: Does this skill install osquery automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. A user must install and configure osquery separately.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Why does this skill need careful use?
faq.answer: It can guide collection of sensitive endpoint data, so authorization and data protection are required.

faq.question: Does it execute attacker tools?
faq.answer: No evidence found. Tool names appear as detection strings inside osquery searches.

faq.question: What platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Linux, macOS, and Windows, subject to osquery table support.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Many basic queries work as a normal user. Sensitive tables often require elevated privileges.
